manifest.name: dsh-lan-access
manifest.description: DSH web plugin: select one concrete local IP for LAN access or bind loopback

bundle.text:
# dsh-lan-access bundle patch
#
# This file is the `dsh.bundle.patch` layer of the package: when installed
# through the official CLI —
#
#   dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-intranet-access-plugin
#
# — the command appends `dsh-lan-access` to `dsh.profile.bundles` and the
# profile boot merges THIS patch (an insert of the host row plus a webserver
# config override) like any manual cordis.patch.yml mount line.

# The host row.
- insert:
    - id: lan-access
      name: 'dsh-lan-access'

# The webserver bind host follows the plugin's persisted setting. This row
# overrides the bundle default (loopback) with an expression that reads the
# live `lanAccess` service provided by the plugin — every webserver fiber
# (re)start evaluates it, so a post-boot user-patch re-apply converges to the
# same host instead of reverting to loopback. The port and TLS retain their invocation expressions; compression uses
# the shipped Web defaults. Every key is restated because a patch row
# replaces the target row's whole config. Drop this row to pin the bind in a later patch layer.
- id: webserver
  config:
    host: !!js ctx.get('lanAccess')?.host ?? '127.0.0.1'
    port: !!js ctx.webStartup.port ?? 3080
    tls: !!js ctx.webStartup.tls
    compression: gzip
    compressionLevel: 1
    compressionThresholdBytes: 1024

readme.text:
A DeepSeek Harness Web plugin that adds an explicit local IP selection and **LAN access** toggle to Settings → General. Requires Node.js 22.19+ or 24+.

> **Tested with [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) `v0.2.1-rc.2`** (the current release) — peers `^0.2.1-rc.2`.

- **On** — binds one selected IPv4 or IPv6 address assigned to this machine. Other devices can use that address; the loopback listener is replaced.
- **Off** — binds `127.0.0.1` (loopback only).
- Wildcard addresses such as `0.0.0.0` and `::` are never used. Loopback, scoped IPv6, link-local IPv4/IPv6 (`169.254.x`, `fe80::/10`), and OS-reported temporary/deprecated IPv6 privacy addresses are excluded from the selector, so it lists only usable LAN endpoints; IPv4 addresses come first.

An older `$DSH_HOME/lan-access.json` containing only `{"enabled": true}` starts on loopback and reports that an address must be selected. The file remains unchanged until you apply a setting. Open the local GUI, select a local IP in Settings → General, and enable LAN access again.

The saved format is now `{"enabled": true, "bindHost": "192.168.1.7"}`. An enabled selection unavailable on the machine fails with an actionable error rather than exposing another interface. To recover after a network change, stop DSH, set `enabled` to `false` in that file, restart locally, and select an available IP.

The DSH web GUI opened from another machine on the same network
(`http://192.168.0.101:3080`):

The **LAN access** toggle in Settings → General, showing the address other
devices can open:

| Half | File | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host | `src/index.ts` | Owns a plugin-local persisted flag (`$DSH_HOME/lan-access.json`), the fenced `/lan-access` JSON route (GET state / POST set), a loopback-only `/lan-access/handoff` that mints the tokenized target URL before the rebind, the bind controller, and the `lanAccess` bind-host service. The webserver row's composed `host` expression reads that service, so every webserver (re)start — boot, toggle, or a post-boot user-patch re-apply — converges to the persisted setting. A toggle restarts the webserver fiber only when the bind differs, using `fiber.update(config, noSave)`: the no-save path keeps the composed tree out of `cordis.yml`, which would otherwise trigger an HMR subtree reload. |
| Client | `src/client/` | Registers the General-settings row (`settings.general.item`, order 15) with a native-styled switch, the concrete IPv4/IPv6 selector, the bound listener URL and copy button, and zh/en copy. A same-origin restart is polled; when the bind moves away from the current origin (which can never reconnect) the row navigates to the tokenized new address automatically, replacing the stuck DSH reconnect loop. |
The route fence accepts loopback, the listener's concrete bind IP, or the deployment's trusted authorities read live from the connection row's resolved config. Cross-site requests are refused.

The built artifacts (`lib/`) are committed, so installation needs no build
step and no modification of the DeepSeek Harness checkout:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/nonmean/dsh-lan-access.git

readme.section: ...or clone and install the local checkout (link: keeps your rebuilds live)
readme.text:
git clone https://github.com/nonmean/dsh-lan-access.git
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-lan-access

dsh web
```

The install appends `dsh-lan-access` to `dsh.profile.bundles`; its
`dsh.bundle.patch` inserts the host row and overrides the webserver row's
`host` with the `lanAccess` service expression. The client half is picked up
by the client-modules scanner automatically. **No harness change is required
for the core feature** — the toggle, the LAN bind, and the live /api trust
fence all ship inside the plugin.

> **Local development** — rebuild with `pnpm build` (or `npm run build`)
> after changing `src/`, then reinstall/restart. The repo's `node_modules`
> mirrors the DSH profile's package farm (TypeScript/tsdown come from the
> harness checkout).

> **Migrating from a manual patch** — remove any `webserver` `host: 0.0.0.0`
> override from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (and the bundle patch layers)
> so the plugin is the single owner of the bind host.

1. Open the local GUI and go to **Settings → General**.
2. Select one available local IPv4 or IPv6 address and enable **LAN access**. Disable LAN access before changing the selection.
3. The listener restarts on the selected address. The original loopback page loses that origin, so the row first asks the loopback-only handoff route for a tokenized target URL, then navigates there automatically: the launch token is exchanged for the new authority's session cookie and the app reconnects for real (no "Reconnecting…" loop). If the handoff is unavailable, the row falls back to showing the new address as a link. A fresh browser still needs the launch token printed by DSH; the displayed URL does not include it. HTTPS listeners retain TLS and use HTTPS URLs; IPv6 literals use brackets.
4. To return to loopback, disable LAN access and open the local address. Disabling from another machine disconnects it.

The selected address is retained when LAN access is disabled. The plugin also supplies a `crypto.randomUUID` polyfill for plain-HTTP LAN pages. The bind controller preserves the resolved listener's port, TLS and compression settings during a toggle. The bundle patch restates the shipped Web defaults because a patch replaces the complete webserver config; deployments that customize these values must restate their complete listener config in a later patch layer.

- **Disabling from a remote machine cannot reconnect that page.** The listener
  returns to `127.0.0.1`, which only exists on the server machine, so the
  remote tab keeps retrying a dead origin. Re-enable from the server machine
  (or the loopback page); the row states this when it applies.
- **The automatic handoff is loopback-only.** The process launch token is
  minted into the target URL only for a loopback page, so it never leaks to a
  remote LAN browser. A bind change started from a non-loopback page (rare —
  the selector is disabled while enabled) falls back to the plain address
  link, and you must supply the launch token printed by `dsh web`.
- **A fresh browser on the new origin needs the launch token.** The URL shown
  in the row omits `?token=`, by design. The automatic handoff carries it only
  for the page that performed the switch.
- **One concrete address, never a wildcard.** The listener binds exactly one
  selected IPv4/IPv6 address; `0.0.0.0`, `::`, link-local, and OS-temporary
  IPv6 addresses are never offered. Change the selection by disabling first.
- **Other tabs on the old origin do not follow.** Only the page that toggles
  navigates to the new origin.

Version 0.4.0 targets DeepSeek Harness `v0.2.1-rc.2` (peers
`^0.2.1-rc.2`). The harness now gates each bundle by its declared DSH peer
range, so this release is skipped on older harnesses — install the plugin
version that matches the harness you run (0.2.0 was the `v0.1.7-rc.2` line).
On `v0.2.1-rc.2+`, upgrade in place:

A full upgrade needs both halves (host + client) and a `dsh web` restart. The
host half now owns its persistence, so the harness settings namespace is no
longer used:

- The toggle value moved to `$DSH_HOME/lan-access.json`. The old
  `lan-access:` section in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml.imported` is not read; flip
  the switch once after upgrading.
- Reinstall (or rebuild `lib/`) so the host and client halves match; the
  client bundle is cached until the next `dsh web`.

readme.section: Remote Settings pages and workspace — no harness change needed
readme.text:
Everything the plugin serves works from a LAN browser with **zero
modification of the DSH checkout**:

readme.section: Remote Settings pages and workspace — no harness change needed
readme.text:
- **The current `/api` gateway trusts the served LAN authority**, so the
  configuration plane (`settings.*`, `credentials.*`) reaches the host
  directly — the Host/Origin fence admits the LAN host and the ordinary
  browser-session auth authenticates it. The Models page provider directory,
  the Plugins configuration cards, and the Language/Appearance rows therefore
  work remotely with no extra hop.
- **On non-loopback origins the client settings persistence degrades to
  memory mode** (surfaces render empty). The browser bundle widens
  `connection.isLoopback` to "loopback OR served LAN authority" at runtime.
  The client entry injects `connection` and is marked
  `dsh.client.immediately`, so its bundle is prefetched and its `apply`
  runs right after the connection row provides the handle — before any
  settings surface (which waits on `remote`) reads
  `remote.$host.isLoopback`. That `inject`-ordered widening is what keeps
  the scope in host mode on a LAN page: without it, a surface that binds early
  sees the unpatched `isLoopback` and its persistence stays memory-mode — the
  plugin configuration cards render nothing.
- **`crypto.randomUUID` does not exist on plain-HTTP LA

The `0.2.1` line added a plugin admission gate: before a profile imports a
bundle, DSH checks that bundle's `peerDependencies` on `@deepseek-ai/dsh` and
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` against the single runtime version and skips the bundle
when any declared range does not match (prereleases participate in range
matching). A plugin that declares only the previous harness line is therefore
silently dropped at startup with a `skipping profile bundle` line. This
release targets the current runtime line — every DSH peer is
`^0.2.1-rc.2` — so the bundle is admitted. The concrete-IP bind also calls
`webServer.getOrigin()`, which first appears in `0.2.1-alpha.3`; the peer
range deliberately excludes the earlier alphas where that method is absent.
The host and client contracts it consumes (`webServer`, `settings`,
`credentials`, `loader`, `connection`, `slots`, `locale`, and the
`settings.general.item` slot) are current for this release. Rebuild `lib/`
after upgrading.

readme.section: Harness API changes this plugin tracks
readme.text:
The harness replaced its standalone, file-backed settings provider with
profile-backed Config forms in `v0.1.7-alpha.1`:

readme.section: Harness API changes this plugin tracks
readme.text:
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings` dropped `settings.register(ns, schema)` /
  `SettingsScope` (and the `dsh-settings-file` package) in favour of
  `SettingsForms`, which projects each plugin entry's volatile `Config`. A
  settings write runs inside an HMR transaction (`configEditor.edit` →
  `hmr.runExclusive`) that reconciles the whole profile. Because this plugin
  must restart the web server to change the bind, routing the toggle through
  that plane would restart the server inside the transaction and taint its
  async context. The plugin therefore persists its own flag
  (`$DSH_HOME/lan-access.json`) and restarts the web server fiber directly
  (`fiber.update(config, true)`), staying off the harness settings plane.

readme.section: Harness API changes this plugin tracks
readme.text:
Earlier, the harness evolved the settings/connection APIs between
`0.1.0-rc.5` and `0.1.5-alpha.1`; the plugin was updated accordingly:

readme.section: Harness API changes this plugin tracks
readme.text:
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings` dropped the `settingsNamespace(ns)` helper —
  `settings.register` / `.update` / `.replace` / `.mutate` now take the raw
  namespace string (validated at runtime and by a compile-time guard).
- The client `ConnectionHandle` no longer carries an `api` member — remote
  methods go through `connection.rpc.call('/api', '<ns>/<method>', …)` — so
  the plugin no longer patches `connection.api.settings.*` /
  `connection.api.credentials.*`.
- The `/api` gateway stopped pinning the configuration plane to loopback: it
  now trusts the served LAN authority, so the settings/credentials RPCs reach
  the host directly. The plugin therefore widens `connection.isLoopback` early
  (via `inject: ['connection']` plus a synchronous patch) to keep the client
  settings persistence in host mode on a LAN page; the fenced `/lan-access/rpc`
  proxy is no longer required for the remote Settings surfaces.

readme.section: Harness API changes this plugin tracks
readme.text:
Remaining loopback-only (hardcoded in the harness, not patchable from a
plugin): `host.pickDirectory` / `host.openPath` (native dialogs and host
file opens) and `llm.discoverModels` (the Models page "discover" button).
The workspace's own add/browse flow does not need them, and chat file
opens route into the sidebar editor.

The host exposes `GET /lan-access/diag` (fenced like the other routes) with
the latest browser boot reports: slot-registration counts, whether the
connection patch is active, and the plugin-item slot ledger. During the first
minute after boot the browser also posts a
2-second poll of the Plugins cards' own injected snapshots (`available`
flags), the slot ledger view, and the declared spec — the exact data that
separates "cards gone", "cards abdicated", and "cards present but rendering
null" when a Settings page misbehaves on a remote machine.

dsh-better-sidebar's trust fence matched the connection row by the wrong
name and read the raw `!!js` config, so its panels (explorer / editor /
terminal / git) only ever accepted loopback. The repo ships the fix as a
profile-level pnpm patch (no harness change):

```sh
./scripts/install-patches.sh web
```

This copies `patches/dsh-better-sidebar.patch` into the profile's
`patches/` directory, registers it under `patchedDependencies` in
`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and runs `pnpm install`.

- Default is **off** (loopback). The DSH launcher itself refuses
  `--host 0.0.0.0` for the same reason: the listener exposes the agent's tools to the selected network. Only enable it on a trusted network.
- The toggle is only reachable through the fenced route, and disabling from a
  remote machine cuts that machine off (expected — re-enable locally).
- `/lan-access/handoff` returns the process launch token, so it refuses every
  non-loopback Host header: a remote LAN page never receives the token and
  cannot mint a cookie for another authority.
- The bind survives plugin reloads and patch re-applies; a full process
  restart re-applies the persisted value at boot.

```sh
pnpm build        # tsdown: lib/index.js (host) + lib/client.js (browser bundle)
pnpm typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
pnpm test         # after build: address validation and controller regressions
```

The client bundle is a `__ModuleLoader__.load` closure-factory artifact (same
format as the DSH monorepo's tsdown client preset); only the frozen
platform-module table words stay external. After changing client code, rebuild
and restart `dsh web` (the client-modules package metadata cache expires only
on restart).
